title: CLI
content:
anyl [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

Formats each file and prints the result. Reads stdin when no file is given.

Options

Option	Description
-w, --write	Overwrite files in place. Can't be combined with --check.
-c, --check	Print the paths of files that would change, and exit with status 1 if any would.
-p, --profile <PROFILE>	A built-in profile name (html, vue) or the path to a profile YAML file. Defaults to the built-in profile for each file's language.
--class-order <CLASS_ORDER>	Order the classes of static class attributes: a built-in class order name (tailwind) or the path to a class order YAML file. Overrides the profile's classOrder.
-l, --language <LANGUAGE>	Language of stdin input: html (default), vue, css, scss, sass, less.
-h, --help	Show help.
-V, --version	Show the version.

Languages

The language of a file is taken from its extension:

Extension	Language	Default profile
.html, .htm	html	html
.vue	vue	vue
.css, .scss, .sass, .less	stylesheet	html (its stylesheet section)

Other extensions are reported as unsupported.

Exit codes

Code	Meaning
0	Success. With --check: no file would change.
1	With --check: at least one file would change.
2	Error: unreadable file, unsupported file type, invalid profile, invalid input or an unknown annealer-* directive.

When several files are given, annealer formats all of them, reports each error, and exits with 2 if any failed.

Examples

anyl src/App.vue                          # print the result
anyl --write src/**/*.vue                 # format in place
anyl --check index.html                   # use in CI
anyl --profile my-profile.yaml page.html  # custom profile
anyl --class-order tailwind src/**/*.vue  # order Tailwind classes
cat App.vue | anyl --language vue         # stdin

title: API Overview
content:
annealer has one Rust core and several ways to call it:

Entry point	For	Reference
anyl	Formatting files from the command line or in CI	CLI
annealer (npm)	Node.js, browsers and bundlers, through WebAssembly	JavaScript API
Profile YAML	Customizing attribute order, layout and stylesheet options	Profile reference

The Rust function annealer::format(input, &Config) is pure: it does no file I/O, which is why the same core runs in the CLI and in WebAssembly.

title: Profile reference
content:
A profile is a YAML file that defines attribute order, layout rules and stylesheet options. The built-in profiles are in crates/annealer/profiles/. # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://github.com/logue/annealer/raw/refs/heads/main/crates/annealer/schema/profile.schema.json schemaVersion: 1 name: my-profile description: My attribute order. normalize: directiveShorthand: true layout: closingBracketNewline: true oneAttributePerLine: true selfClosing: void: always contentNewline: {} groups: - name: global match: [id] - name: class match: [class] - name: other fallback: true - name: events match: ['on*'] stylesheet: declarationOrder: smacss vendorPrefix: start The JSON Schema (draft-07) is at crates/annealer/schema/profile.schema.json. With the modeline above and the YAML extension, VS Code validates and completes profiles. Unknown keys are errors everywhere in a profile, so typos never go unnoticed. Top level Key Type Required Description schemaVersion 1 yes Profile format version. name string yes Profile name. description string Human-readable summary. normalize object Attribute name rewrites. layout object Start-tag layout rules. groups array yes Attribute groups in output order. stylesheet object Stylesheet formatting. Omit it to leave stylesheets untouched. classOrder string | object Class order for static class attributes. Omit it to keep classes in their order. normalize Rewrites applied before classification. Key Type Default Description directiveShorthand boolean false v-bind:foo → :foo, v-on:click → @click. hyphenateComponentProps boolean false camelCase attribute names on component tags → kebab-case. Native SVG/MathML elements are excluded. layout See Layout for details. Key Type Default Description closingBracketNewline boolean false Put the closing bracket of a multiline start tag on its own line. oneAttributePerLine boolean false One attribute per line in a multiline start tag. selfClosing.void always | never | preserve preserve Void elements:
or
. selfClosing.normal always | never | preserve preserve Empty non-void elements (
). Vue templates only. selfClosing.component always | never | preserve preserve Empty components (). Vue templates only. contentNewline object off Put the content of a multiline element on lines of its own. {} turns it on with the defaults. contentNewline.ignore string[] pre, textarea, inline elements Elements left alone, with everything inside them. Element names match case-insensitively; component names match exactly. contentNewline.allowEmptyLines boolean false Keep blank lines before and after the content. groups Groups are listed in output order. Exactly one group must be the fallback, and group names must be unique. Key Type Default Description name string – Unique group name. Required. match string[] – Patterns: an exact name or a prefix ending in *. Required unless fallback: true. sort source | alphabetical | listed source Order within the group: as written, by key, or by the order of match. fallback boolean false Receives every attribute that matches no pattern. spreadSafe boolean false Attributes in this group may move across a v-bind="object" spread. Only for compile-time directives. Patterns are matched against normalized, lowercased keys: foo for foo/:foo/v-bind:foo, v-on:click for @click, v-slot:name for #name, with modifiers stripped. An exact name beats any prefix, and a longer prefix beats a shorter one. See Attribute order. stylesheet See Stylesheets for details. Key Type Default Description declarationOrder smacss | concentric | alphabetical – Property order. Without it, declarations are not reordered. declarationOrderGroupBy non-declaration | non-declaration-and-empty-line non-declaration How declarations are split into runs that are sorted separately. vendorPrefix alongside | start alongside start puts vendor-prefixed declarations first in each run, alphabetically. styleAttribute boolean false Also order declarations in static style attributes. malva object – Other malva options, passed through. stylesheet.malva accepts malva's own options, such as printWidth, useTabs, indentWidth, lineBreak, hexCase, hexColorLength, quotes, trailingComma, formatComments and the *.preferSingleLine options. declarationOrder and declarationOrderGroupBy belong to stylesheet itself, not to malva. Unknown malva keys are rejected. quotes defaults to prefer-single in annealer (malva's own default is always-double); see Quotes. classOrder The order of the classes in static class attributes (see Class order): a built-in class order name (tailwind), or a class order profile written inline. The CLI's --class-order and the JavaScript classOrder option override it. classOrder: tailwind Class order profiles A class order profile is a YAML file of its own, passed with --class-order or classOrder, or written inline under a profile's classOrder. The JSON Schema is crates/annealer/schema/class-order.schema.json; the built-in one is crates/annealer/class-orders/tailwind.yaml. Key Type Default Description schemaVersion 1 – Required. Format version. name string – Required. Class order name. description string – Human-readable summary. unknown start | end start Where classes no rule matches go, in source order. removeDuplicates boolean false Drop repeated classes, keeping the first. important string – Marker stripped from the start or end of a utility before matching (!). arbitraryProperties boolean false Classes of the form [property:value] set property. variants object – separator (e.g. :) and order: variant patterns by rank, lowest first. A list entry gives its patterns the same rank. propertyOrder string[] – Required. CSS properties in output order. values map of pattern list – Value sets for {name} in patterns. number is built in. rules array – Required. match (patterns), properties (from propertyOrder) and optional count (number of declarations, if different). A class with a variant that no pattern matches is unknown. Rules may only name properties listed in propertyOrder; anything else is an error.

title: Attribute order
content:
Tokenizer: no DOM

annealer does not build a DOM or XML tree. It finds each start tag (<tagname … > or />) and splits the attribute list into name/value pairs, keeping only the quote style.

This works the same way for plain HTML and for Vue's non-XML syntax (@click, #default, v-bind:[dynamic]). It also avoids side effects of DOM- or XML-based parsing, such as collapsing whitespace or lowercasing tag and attribute names.

Raw-text elements, comments, {{ }} interpolations, SFC <script> blocks, custom blocks and <template lang="…"> with a non-HTML language are skipped.

Classification

Each attribute is classified by its normalized key:

Written as	Key
foo, :foo, v-bind:foo	foo
@click, v-on:click	v-on:click
#item, v-slot:item	v-slot:item
@click.stop, :foo.camel	modifiers stripped

A profile is a list of groups in output order. Each group has match patterns: an exact name, or a prefix ending in *. An attribute goes to the group whose pattern fits it most specifically: an exact name beats any prefix, and a longer prefix beats a shorter one. Attributes that match nothing go to the single fallback group.

Inside a group, the order is set by sort:

source: as written (default).

alphabetical: by key.

listed: by the order of the match patterns.

HTML profile

#	Group	Attributes	Sort
1	global	id	
2	class	class	
3	supplementary	alt, title, placeholder	listed
4	semantic	type, href, src, srcset	listed
5	key-value	name, value, content	listed
6	dimensions	width, height	listed
7	other (fallback)	state attributes such as disabled, checked, readonly	source
8	aria-role	role	
9	aria-name	aria-label, aria-labelledby	listed
10	aria-description	aria-describedby, aria-description, aria-details	listed
11	aria-property	other aria-*	source
12	aria-state	aria-busy, aria-checked, aria-current, aria-disabled, aria-expanded, aria-grabbed, aria-hidden, aria-invalid, aria-pressed, aria-selected	source
13	data	data-*	alphabetical
14	events	on*	source

Why this order:

Supplementary attributes come right after id/class. They describe the element for a human reader. id and class stay together at the front because that is the common idiom.

ARIA goes near the end. It carries extra metadata for assistive technology that alt/title can't express. It is not the primary description of the element.

ARIA follows WAI-ARIA: role → accessible name → description → properties → states.

data-* is alphabetical because no semantic order exists for it.

Vue profile

The Vue profile follows the default order of eslint-plugin-vue's vue/attributes-order, so its output always satisfies that rule:

#	Tier	Attributes
1	Definition	is, v-is
2	List rendering	v-for
3	Conditionals	v-if, v-else-if, v-else, v-show, v-cloak
4	Render modifiers	v-pre, v-once
5	Global	id
6	Unique / slot	ref, key, slot, v-slot*
7	Two-way binding	v-model*
8a	Other directives	other v-*
8b	Other attributes	the HTML profile's groups from class to data (see above)
9	Events	v-on* (@…)
10	Content	v-html, v-text

Tier 8 is split into other directives first, then other attributes. This matches OTHER_DIRECTIVES → OTHER_ATTR in vue/attributes-order. The HTML sub-ordering applies inside the other-attributes tier.

<!-- Input -->
<MyItem
  @click="select"
  :class="{ active }"
  class="item"
  v-for="item in items"
  :key="item.id"
  aria-label="Item"
  v-bind:title="item.name"
  :itemName="item.name"
/>

<!-- Output -->
<MyItem
  v-for="item in items"
  :key="item.id"
  class="item"
  :class="{ active }"
  :title="item.name"
  :item-name="item.name"
  aria-label="Item"
  @click="select"
/>

Same-name clustering

Because classification uses the normalized key, the static and bound forms of one attribute get the same key and stay together. The first occurrence of a key sets the position of its cluster. No special-case logic is needed.

For class, the static form goes before the bound form (class="item" :class="{ active }").

For other names, the cluster keeps the source order. Vue merges style and the later declaration wins. For other duplicate names it keeps only one of them. Reordering them could change behavior.

v-model is never clustered with a plain attribute of the same name (value="x" v-model="y"). Its key is v-model, not value, and it stays in its own tier because two-way binding is a different concept.

v-bind spreads

v-bind="object" is a boundary. Attributes are never moved across a spread, because that can change which value wins when the object is merged.

The exception is groups marked spreadSafe. These are compile-time directives (is, v-for, v-if/…, v-pre/v-once, custom directives) that never merge with the spread object, so they can be moved across it. Everything else stays inside its segment.

Normalization

The Vue profile enables two rewrites, which run before classification:

directiveShorthand: v-bind:foo → :foo, v-on:click → @click.

hyphenateComponentProps: camelCase attribute names on component tags → kebab-case (:itemName → :item-name). Native SVG and MathML elements are not affected.

title: Design decisions
content:
Architecture

annealer (core)  pure function: format(input: &str, config: &Config)
                   -> Result<String, FormatError>
                 No file I/O. Builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown.
                 Uses malva for CSS/SCSS/Sass/Less declaration order.

anyl (CLI)       File I/O and argument parsing; calls the core.

annealer (npm)   WebAssembly build of the core with a TypeScript wrapper.

One crate. The core and the CLI live in one crate (crates/annealer) for now. It will be split into a workspace only when a real need appears, to avoid premature abstraction. The CLI's clap dependency is behind the default cli feature, so the library builds for WebAssembly with --no-default-features.

Profiles are YAML, not code. HTML, Vue and future profiles are data. Each profile has schemaVersion, because the format is as much a public API as the Rust function signature.

Strict validation. Unknown keys are rejected when the profile is parsed, so typos surface immediately. A JSON Schema (draft-07) is provided for editor support. Two rules that draft-07 can't express (exactly one fallback group, unique group names) are checked only by the loader.

malva is pinned loosely (0.16), in line with the library dependency policy used in other projects.

The npm package embeds the WebAssembly binary as base64 instead of shipping a separate .wasm file. The cost is about 33% more bytes before compression. In return, format() is synchronous and needs no bundler or loader setup.

Decisions made during implementation

HTML profile order. The original table had no place for unmatched attributes or for alt/title. The agreed order is id → class → supplementary (alt, title, placeholder) → semantic (type, href, src, srcset) → key-value (name, value, content) → dimensions (width, height) → other (state: disabled, checked, …) → ARIA → data → events. The Vue profile uses the same order inside its other-attributes tier.

Static before bound applies to class only. For other names, the cluster keeps the source order, because Vue merges style with the later declaration winning and keeps only one value for other duplicates.

spreadSafe groups. Compile-time directives never merge with a v-bind spread object, so they may move across spreads. Everything else stays inside its segment.

One attribute per line in multiline tags. Otherwise reordering could put two attributes on one line. This matches the multiline default of vue/max-attributes-per-line and can be turned off with layout.oneAttributePerLine.

Vue tier 8 is split into other directives, then other attributes, as in vue/attributes-order (OTHER_DIRECTIVES → OTHER_ATTR).

void: always differs from vue/html-self-closing's default (html.void: never). Projects that keep that ESLint rule need to align one side.

contentNewline is on in the HTML profile too. Whitespace at the start and end of block-level content isn't rendered, and the ignore list covers the elements where it could be.

Vendor-prefixed declarations go first (vendorPrefix: start), so the standard property is declared last and wins. See Stylesheets.

Resolved questions

v-model and a plain value: never clustered. The key v-model differs from value.

Profile strictness: unknown keys are rejected at parse time.

malva version: loose range 0.16.

Open items

Upgrade raffia to 0.13 once malva does (malva 0.16 still uses raffia 0.12).

Svelte profile.

Value ordering for static class attributes (Tailwind approximation, Bootstrap proposal).

Library profiles, profile composition (extends) and per-tag or per-component overrides.

Fixtures taken from real projects, in addition to the hand-written ones.

title: Library profiles
content:
Planned. The discovery policy below is decided; the implementation is not done yet.

annealer will support rule settings specific to a library (a UI kit, a CSS framework). These reuse the existing profile mechanism instead of adding code branches:

attribute groups,

layout.selfClosing per element kind,

normalization options,

class value order (see Value ordering).

The mechanisms are kept general and data-driven, so a library profile can extend or override them. This will likely need profile composition (extends) and per-tag or per-component overrides.

Discovery policy

Detected by annealer.yaml in the package

A package provides a library profile when its package root contains an annealer.yaml. The presence of that file is the only signal. annealer doesn't use package-name conventions and doesn't guess from the package contents.

Direct dependencies only, by default

Only the project's direct dependencies are scanned. A transitive dependency is included only when a library author opts in explicitly. For example, a UI kit built on Bootstrap can declare in its own annealer.yaml that it carries Bootstrap's profile.

A package somewhere deep in the dependency tree doesn't mean the project's markup uses its classes.

Detection and application are separate

Detection only finds candidates and reports them. A profile is applied only when the user names it explicitly in their config.

Installing or updating a dependency must never change annealer's output by itself.

Bootstrap

For Bootstrap, the plan is to propose the mechanism to the Bootstrap project (v6 is in development) with a draft profile, so that Bootstrap owns its class order. This requires a stable, documented profile format first.

title: Value ordering
content:
Both are implemented: static style attributes (opt-in, see Stylesheets) and class values with a swappable class order (see Class order), with a built-in tailwind order. A Bootstrap profile is not written yet. This page records the principles behind them.

Attribute order is one axis. The order of the values inside an attribute is another. The need isn't specific to Tailwind: any class-based CSS framework (Bootstrap, Tailwind, a project's own utility set) benefits from a fixed class order, for the same diff-stability reason as attributes.

Principles

Static values only

Bound attributes (:class, :style, v-bind:*) hold expressions, not values. annealer never looks inside them.

This differs from eslint-plugin-tailwindcss (classnames-order) and prettier-plugin-tailwindcss, which also sort string literals inside :class expressions and clsx()-style calls.

A library-agnostic mechanism, with library-specific profiles

The class order is plain profile data, like attribute groups, not a code branch. This is the first concrete case of library profiles.

The library owns its class order

A framework's canonical class order is a design decision of that framework, not of annealer. annealer provides the mechanism and the profile format.

Bootstrap: annealer proposes the mechanism upstream, with a draft profile (Bootstrap 6 is in development), so that Bootstrap itself defines and maintains the order.

Tailwind: the order is already defined by Tailwind's engine. annealer ships it as built-in YAML (tailwind), generated from Tailwind and checked against it. It follows the spec of eslint-plugin-tailwindcss classnames-order, except that duplicates are kept (see below).

The profile format is a public contract

Third parties are expected to write and ship profiles. Before the proposal, schemaVersion, the JSON Schema and the format documentation must be stable. Profiles distributed outside annealer also need a loading path (for example, extends resolving a file shipped in a package).

An approximate, self-contained order

The official Tailwind order is derived from each project's own Tailwind build (v4 @theme and custom utilities, v3 tailwind.config.js). Only Tailwind itself can compute it. annealer defines the order in YAML instead:

close to the official order for standard utilities,

custom utilities are not known,

no JavaScript runtime is required.

Never change meaning

Reordering classes doesn't change CSS semantics. Duplicate classes are kept (removing them is a lint concern), and unknown classes are never dropped.

Design

Classes are ranked by the CSS properties they set, with Tailwind's comparison: unknown classes, variants, the first differing property in a property order, the number of properties, then the name. Properties are library-agnostic, so a Bootstrap profile can use the same format (d-flex sets display, mt-3 sets margin-top).

Variants (Tailwind's md:, hover:) are a separate axis: a separator and a ranked list of variant patterns.

Patterns are richer than attribute patterns: * anywhere and {name} value sets, with the most specific match winning. text-center, text-lg and text-red-500 resolve to different rules.

The class order is its own profile, not part of the attribute profile, so it can be combined with any attribute profile: --class-order, the classOrder option, or classOrder in a profile.

Resolved questions

Where unknown classes go: unknown: start (Tailwind's order) or end.

Whitespace inside a class value is preserved: classes move between the existing separators, as eslint-plugin-tailwindcss does.

Open questions

Infix breakpoints (Bootstrap's col-md-6, d-lg-none) are not a separate axis yet. A profile can only rank them through patterns.

How attribute profiles compose (for example extends: vue). This also serves library-specific attribute rules.

title: Class order
content:
annealer can reorder the classes inside static class attributes. The order comes from a class order profile, a YAML file separate from the attribute profile, so it can be swapped for another library's order. It is off by default. Turn it on with a class order name or file: anyl --class-order tailwind src/**/*.vue anyl --class-order ./my-classes.yaml index.html format(source, { language: 'vue', classOrder: 'tailwind' }); An attribute profile can also name one with classOrder. --class-order and the classOrder option override it. Built-in: tailwind The built-in tailwind class order follows the order that eslint-plugin-tailwindcss (classnames-order) and prettier-plugin-tailwindcss apply. Both take it from the Tailwind CSS compiler.
annealer doesn't run Tailwind. The order is data, generated from Tailwind CSS 4.3 with its default theme by scripts/generate-tailwind-order.mjs. The same script writes a test corpus of 3,000 class lists sorted by Tailwind itself, and annealer's output matches all of them. Differences from running Tailwind: Your own theme and utilities aren't known. A custom color (bg-brand-500) is ordered like a theme color, because a value that matches no other rule falls back to the color rule. A custom utility (@utility) is an unknown class. Duplicates are kept. eslint-plugin-tailwindcss removes them by default (removeDuplicates). Removing classes is a lint concern, so the built-in profile keeps them. A class order with removeDuplicates: true removes them. Only static class attributes. :class bindings and clsx()-style calls are expressions, and annealer never reads them. How classes are ordered Classes no rule matches (card, js-toggle) go first, in their source order (unknown: end puts them last). Classes without variants come first. Classes with variants follow, by the ranks of their variants (variants.order). The highest rank decides, like comparing bit masks. Then by the CSS properties a class sets: the first property that differs, by its position in propertyOrder. Then more properties first (count). Then by name, with runs of digits compared as numbers (p-2 before p-10). This is the comparison Tailwind uses. Nothing in it is specific to Tailwind: any utility library can describe its classes by the properties they set. What changes in the markup Whitespace stays in place: classes move between the existing separators, so multi-line class lists keep their line breaks. Values with template syntax ({{ }}, {% %}, , ${}) and unquoted values are left as written. Disable directives apply as for attributes. Writing a class order # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://github.com/logue/annealer/raw/refs/heads/main/crates/annealer/schema/class-order.schema.json schemaVersion: 1 name: my-utilities unknown: end propertyOrder: [display, margin, padding, color] values: size: [sm, md, lg] rules: - match: [d-*] properties: [display] - match: ['m-{number}', 'm-{size}', mx-auto] properties: [margin] - match: ['p-{number}'] properties: [padding] - match: [text-*] properties: [color] match patterns: * matches any run of characters; {name} matches one entry of a value set in values. {number} (a decimal number) is built in. The most specific pattern wins: an exact name, then the most literal characters, then the most value sets. A modifier after / (bg-red-500/50) is ignored when the class without it matches better. See the class order reference for every key. builtinClassOrder('tailwind') in the JavaScript API returns the built-in YAML as a starting point.

content: Some code must keep its exact form, for example a third-party snippet or a legacy order kept on purpose. title: Layout
content:
Reordering attributes can break the original line layout of a tag. The layout section of a profile defines how tags are laid out afterwards. Each rule mirrors an eslint-plugin-vue rule, so projects that keep those rules get consistent results. Both built-in profiles turn all of these rules on. closingBracketNewline Equivalent to vue/html-closing-bracket-newline. The closing bracket of a multiline start tag goes on its own line. A start tag whose attributes fit on one line keeps > on that line (singleline: never). oneAttributePerLine Equivalent to the multiline default of vue/max-attributes-per-line. In a start tag whose attributes span several lines, each attribute goes on its own line. This is needed because reordering could otherwise put two attributes on one line if attributes kept their original line positions.
selfClosing Equivalent to vue/html-self-closing. Set per element kind, each to always, never or preserve: Kind Example Built-in html Built-in vue void
always always normal
– always component – always normal and component apply in Vue templates only. In plain HTML,
is an unclosed start tag. Whitespace-only content counts as empty, except in pre and textarea. SFC top-level blocks (

title: Getting started
content:
annealer has three entry points that share the same Rust core: anyl: the command-line tool. annealer (npm): a JavaScript API backed by WebAssembly. annealer (Rust crate): the pure format() function. CLI Build the CLI from the repository (the npm package and crate are not published yet): cargo install --path crates/annealer Then format files: anyl src/App.vue # print the result anyl --write src/**/*.vue # format in place anyl --check index.html # exit 1 if a file would change anyl --profile my-profile.yaml page.html Supported inputs: .html, .htm, .vue, .css, .scss, .sass, .less. The language is detected from the extension, and each language uses its matching built-in profile unless --profile is given. See CLI for all options. JavaScript format('Home'); // => 'Home' format(source, { language: 'vue' }); format(source, { language: 'html', profile: yamlText }); format() is synchronous. The WebAssembly binary is embedded in the package, so no loader or bundler setup is needed. See JavaScript API. Example Input:

Output with the html profile:

id and class come first, then supplementary (placeholder), semantic (type), key-value (name) and state (required) attributes, then ARIA. The multiline tag gets one attribute per line, and the closing bracket goes on its own line. The void element becomes . Profiles Two profiles are built in: Profile Used for Summary html .html, .css, .scss, .sass, .less Semantic order for plain HTML. vue .vue vue/attributes-order tiers plus annealer's sub-ordering. To customize, start from a built-in profile (builtinProfile('vue') in JavaScript, or crates/annealer/profiles/*.yaml) and pass your YAML with --profile or the profile option. See Profile reference.

title: Introduction
content: annealer is a formatter that reorders HTML and Vue template attributes by their semantic meaning. It also reorders declarations in stylesheets (CSS, SCSS, Sass, Less). The order is defined by a swappable YAML profile, not hard-coded. Home Home annealer is under active development. The npm package is not published yet, and the profile format can still change before it is declared stable. Why attribute order matters Order is a code-review problem, not a cosmetic one When several contributors edit the same component over time, attributes are added, removed and rewritten. Without a fixed rule, the attribute list gets reshuffled, and diffs pull in lines that didn't really change. A stable, rule-based order keeps a diff limited to what actually changed, which lowers the cost of review. Attributes carry different semantic weight HTML attributes are not an unordered set of strings: Some define what an element is (is, a component name). Some control its state or behavior (v-if, v-model, disabled, width/height). Some supplement its meaning for a human reader (title, alt). Some propagate meaning to external systems such as assistive technology (aria-*). Sorting alphabetically, or keeping the typed order, hides this structure. annealer orders attributes so that an element's semantic structure is visible in the source. The grouping is not an arbitrary preference. The WAI-ARIA specification itself splits aria-* attributes into properties (which don't change during use) and states (which do). annealer uses this split. Stylesheets deserve the same treatment CSS properties also have roles: layout, appearance, state-dependent presentation. The same "order by meaning" principle applies to declaration order. Relation to vue/attributes-order The Vue.js Style Guide already defines a priority list for attributes, and eslint-plugin-vue implements it as vue/attributes-order. annealer's Vue profile starts from the same default order, so projects that move away from ESLint keep the same result. On top of that baseline, annealer adds: Same-name clustering: the static and bound forms of one attribute stay together (class next to :class). ARIA sub-ordering: role → name → description → property → state, following the WAI-ARIA properties/states split. Plain HTML support, for projects without Vue templates. Stylesheet declaration order, delegated to malva. annealer is not a rival to vue/attributes-order. It inherits its design and extends it. For teams that replace ESLint with rslint or oxlint, it keeps this one piece of functionality alive. Why a new tool Biome, rslint, oxlint, oxfmt and markup_fmt were evaluated. None of them reorders Vue/HTML attributes by meaning: Tool Status Biome (useSortedAttributes, HTML) Fixed, undocumented category split; doesn't place non-directive attributes such as id the way the Vue Style Guide does; shares infrastructure with a known regression (duplicated/dropped attributes). rslint No plans to support Vue (maintainer decision). oxlint Vue rules are about correctness only; no attribute-order rule. oxfmt Can't reach template markup by design. markup_fmt Formats Vue/Svelte/Astro templates, but has no option to reorder attributes. CSS property order is the exception: malva already has a configurable declarationOrder, so annealer delegates to it. What annealer adds is the semantic attribute grouping. Nothing else is built from zero. Scope Attribute reordering in HTML and in Vue 3 SFC
